name: Stonemasons Guild
summary: Stormwind's rebuilding ended in a bitter dispute between the Stonemasons Guild and the House of Nobles. Deadly riots followed, and the guild was dissolved. Its members went into exile, and the scattered artisans' fate remains a mystery.

sections.title: Architects of the Realm
sections.body: Edwin VanCleef led the Stonemasons Guild as its elected Guildmaster. Its masons matched the skill of the dwarven Royal Stonecutters Union. After the First and Second Wars left Stormwind in ruins, the House of Nobles hired them to rebuild the city and restore the capital to its ancient grandeur.

sections.title: Toil and Betrayal
sections.body: For years, VanCleef and his craftsmen worked across Elwynn. They raised Stormwind Keep's soaring spires and the Cathedral of Light's great arches. Then royal finances collapsed under debts from military campaigns in the south. Guided by aristocratic politics, the House of Nobles refused to pay the agreed salaries and fees. When VanCleef sought restitution, the nobles disbanded the guild without its consent. Fury spread among the laborers who had bled to rebuild the city.

sections.title: Blood in the Streets
sections.body: The wage dispute became violent unrest throughout Stormwind. The Crown cracked down, capturing key conspirators, including VanCleef's lieutenant, Bazil Thredd. VanCleef and hundreds of ruined stonemasons fled into the Westfall countryside. Branded traitors and forced into exile, the desperate artisans turned their trade union into the militant Defias Brotherhood.

sections.title: The Hidden Hand
sections.body: Lady Katrana Prestor, an advisor to the royal court, fed discord between the nobility and the builders. She persuaded the aristocracy that the Stonemasons' bills were extortionate and their work shoddy. At the same time, she provoked the craftsmen into open rebellion. By paralyzing Stormwind with strife and cutting off supplies to Westfall, the black dragon Onyxia fractured the kingdom from within.

faq.answer: The Stonemasons Guild was an association of human artisans, architects, and stonecutters led by elected Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef. Its members earned renown rebuilding Stormwind City after the Second War.

faq.q: Why did the Stonemasons Guild become the Defias Brotherhood?
faq.answer: The House of Nobles refused to pay the guild's wages after Stormwind's rebuilding, amid crippling debt and court intrigue. Deadly protests drove the workers into exile, where they formed the Defias Brotherhood to claim their stolen wealth by force.

faq.q: Who was the leader of the Stonemasons Guild?
faq.answer: Edwin VanCleef was the guild's elected Guildmaster. Under his leadership, the masons became known for their stonework before he was exiled and founded the Defias Brotherhood.

faq.q: What notable structures did the Stonemasons build?
faq.answer: The guild rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War, including the Cathedral of Light and Stormwind Keep.

faq.q: Did all the Stonemasons join the Defias Brotherhood?
aliases: did any stonemasons stay in stormwind
faq.answer: Some stonemasons did not join the rebellion. Master craftsman Baros Alexston broke with Edwin VanCleef, remained in Stormwind, and became City Architect. His former guildmates hated him for it.

faq.q: What happened during the Stonemason riots?
faq.answer: When the nobles disbanded the guild instead of paying it, stonemasons rioted in Stormwind's streets. The Crown captured VanCleef's lieutenant Bazil Thredd, while VanCleef and the other masons fled to Westfall.

faq.q: Who was Bazil Thredd in the Stonemasons Guild?
faq.answer: Bazil Thredd was Edwin VanCleef's trusted assistant and chief lieutenant in the guild. The Crown captured him after the riots, and he remains locked inside the Stormwind Stockade.

angles.text: Stormwind's beautiful white stone recalls a bitter tragedy within the kingdom and the cost of aristocratic pride for human travelers.
Dwarven masons respected the Stonemasons Guild. Its precision and towering ramparts rivaled those of Ironforge's Royal Stonecutters Union.
VanCleef's cunning reached far: master tradesmen became deadly highwaymen, lockpicks, and assassins.
The guild's collapse left Westfall's breadbasket defenseless and overrun by outlaws. The Alliance's supply lines were strained just outside the capital.
